## The challenge

Press **NOD** in Home Assistant, and a physical lamp nods its head.

That simple gesture teaches something much bigger: how an Open Engineering
declaration can travel through abstractions, a Pico digital twin, a runtime,
an event, an edge adapter, and an electrical interface — until the physical
world actually changes.

> *Declare a meaningful capability in Open Engineering and follow it all the way
> until the physical world changes.*

## Why this course exists

Everything you have learned separately — Kubernetes, MiniKube, Crossplane,
Pico, Manifold, events, Home Assistant — is a single, cooperating system here.
This is a **capstone**: it composes what you already know instead of teaching
each technology again.

It is also the academy's first **cyber-physical** course. Open Engineering is
not only a way to describe and operate *software*; it is a method for composing
*cyber-physical* systems.

## The conceptual journey

```
Human Intent
     ↓
Home Assistant
     ↓
Open Engineering Capability
     ↓
Pico Digital Twin
     ↓
Manifold Runtime
     ↓
Open Engineering Event
     ↓
Edge Adapter
     ↓
ESP32
     ↓
74HCT245
     ↓
AX-12A
     ↓
Mechanical Lamp Head
     ↓
Physical Motion
```

The final proof that the architecture works is:

**The lamp nods.**

## Learning path

The course is a single forward build wrapped by a challenge and a capstone:

- Module 0 — **The Challenge**: see the finished result before building it.
- Modules 1–2 — **The physical system and the capability**: meet the hardware,
  then the *semantic* capability it exposes.
- Modules 3–4 — **Digital twin and simulation**: model the actuator as a Pico,
  run it without hardware.
- Modules 5–7 — **Compose, run, bring alive**: Crossplane, MiniKube, Manifold.
- Modules 8–9 — **The edge**: the ESP32 adapter and the physical AX-12A.
- Modules 10–12 — **Expose, trace, and nod**: Home Assistant, observability,
  and the capstone.

## Reuse-first

This course deliberately does **not** repeat your earlier courses. It links to
them:

- [Kubernetes](../kubernetes/) — the local cluster and MiniKube foundation.
- [Crossplane](../crossplane/) — XRDs, XRs, Compositions, providers.
- [Pico](../pico/) — Rules, Parser, Composer, Pico digital entities.
- [Manifold](../manifold/) — the Pico runtime execution environment.
- [Hello Pico on Home Assistant](../../labs/hello-pico-home-assistant/) — Home
  Assistant as a control surface.

The **prerequisites** page lists exactly what you need, and the
**architecture** page is the map you will follow.
